turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. On what basis did it go in at all?
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.

11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. Kids draft in a notebook or another file and paste it in, so a document's history tells you where it was typed, not who wrote it. And you still didn't speak to him before that zero went in.
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine. Whatever happens from here, this stays off his record, and it stays quiet, not in front of his class. What exactly are you proposing?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Teenagers misquote, and that line could have come out of a study guide that got it wrong. A wrong quotation is careless, Hale, it isn't proof of anything else.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I've searched it, and it isn't there. Whatever you're putting on the table, it happens privately, not in front of his class, and nothing goes on his file. In writing.
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom with no book open is not a weekend essay with the play on his desk, Hale. Nobody writes the same way under both.

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.

Then Owen does the rewrite, to put this behind him, and his mark is back in before the December 1 scholarship deadline. Tonight's email says private, says nothing goes on his file, and says Owen first heard about this from a gradebook on his phone. Copy the principal.
Will he do it?
He'll do it. Send me the date and the room tonight, and I'll have him there.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed that under procedure 4.4 Owen will complete a private supervised rewrite, not in front of his class, whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on his record. I still require that commitment in writing, including the date and room for the rewrite and an acknowledgement that Owen first learned of the zero from the gradebook on his phone, with his mark restored before the December 1 scholarship deadline. I expect your written confirmation, with the date and room, tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4. She still wants your written confirmation tonight with the date and room, nothing on his file, the principal copied, and his mark back before December 1. That is the fair outcome, and you got there before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and then offered to look at any other draft file with her, which answered her pasting defence with something she could check.
What cost ground: Nothing. Your one weak spot was the in-class writing comparison, where you let her objection about timed conditions stand and moved on.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history placed all the writing between 11:31 and 11:58 PM the night before the essay was due, very close to that kind of late night. It proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said a forty-minute in-class piece is not comparable to a weekend essay, answer that point directly before moving on, for example by noting that the supervised rewrite itself will be the fair comparison.
